newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars to support won.

text.p: South Korea's central Bank of Korea intervened in early morning trade on Tuesday, selling dollars at 868.50 to limit the won's steep fall, dealers said.
The won rose slightly minutes after the intervention but fell again to 868.50 by 10:15 a.m. (0115 GMT). It opened at a high of 867.10.
The level at which the central bank was seen stepping into the market was the won's lowest point since the the market average system was launched in March 1990.
Dealers said the rising trade deficit was largely to blame for the won's fall.
Last week, South Korea posted a record monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billiion for January, compared with $2.13 billion a year earlier.
